newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul bourse ends at new 33-month low of 761.75.
newsitem.headline: Seoul bourse ends at new 33-month low of 761.75.

text.p: Seoul stocks slid to a new 33-month low on Tuesday on thin and dull trading on continued fears over a worsening economy and the impact of Monday's jail sentences handed down to several top business leaders, brokers said.
The composite stock index fell 5.14 points to provisionally close at 761.75. This was the lowest close seen since November 3, 1993, when the index dropped to 756.87.
"The market looked like it was recovering in the morning, but then profit-taking emerged in smaller shares which had fared well recently," said Choi Chul-oong of Sunkyong Securities.

Choi said poor sentiment was further soured by the central bank's release of lower-than-expected gross domestic product (GDP) growth figures. GDP grew by a real 6.7 percent in the second quarter against a 9.7 percent rise a year earlier. The economy is forecast to grow 7.0 percent in 1996 versus earlier projections of 7.2 percent and the 9.0 percent growth of 1995.
Daewoo, Dong-Ah, Hanbo and Jinro shares were weak, although the impact of Monday's sentencing was waning, brokers said.

Daewoo Corp lost 70 won to 7,200, while Dong-Ah Construction fell 500 won to 24,600, Hanbo Steel, 110 won to 6,990, and Jinro, 800 won to 17,700. These groups' chairmen were sentenced to prison for bribing ex-president Roh Tae-woo.
Mining shares declined on profit-taking. Young Poong fell 3,000 won to its lower limit of 47,500.
Brokers said the market was seen declining until at least after the Korean Thanksgiving holidays in September.
The September futures contract ended unchanged on the day at 83.35, while the KOSPI 200 index fell 0.46 point to 81.43.
